In Quzhou County, I will keep my land in the crop pattern I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. I will do that because this is still the main local system, it fits our warm-temperate North China Plain climate, and it matches the water pattern here: most rain comes in the maize season, while wheat needs the irrigation. I will not spread my land into many crops, because I would rather keep one simple grain rotation that I know how to manage, can get seed and machine service for, and can sell without trouble. For wheat, I will stay with an improved local wheat variety and manage water carefully, because official Hebei and Ministry of Agriculture materials still show wheat-maize rotation as the core system in Quzhou and give wheat nutrient ranges around N 15-20, P 8-12, K 6-10 kg/mu with several irrigations; for maize, I will use hybrid seed and a lighter irrigation plan because summer rain usually carries more of the crop and official maize ranges are about N 15-20, P 6-8 or 6-10, K 8-10 kg/mu with supplemental watering as needed. I am assuming I farm 10 mu total, since my land area was not given. Sources I used: China Agricultural University Quzhou Experimental Station on Quzhou-wide promotion of the wheat-maize integrated system, the Ministry of Agriculture wheat and maize water-fertilizer technical plans, and the Hebei 2024 leading varieties/technologies notice: https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/2/25/art_46232_1012984.html , https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/zxfb/202504/t20250407_6472869.htm , https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/zxfb/202504/t20250410_6473061.htm , https://www.weihengag.com/home/article/detail/id/22747
